summary.title: Dagoba: An In-Memory Graph Database
summary.one_liner: You learn how to design a small in-memory graph database in JavaScript, covering vertices, edges, a Gremlin-style chainable query API, and lazy versus eager query evaluation.
keywords: call by need vs call by value
takeaways: Graphs model connections naturally, and chained traversal calls like Thor.parents.parents can replace deep SQL subqueries.
A graph can be built as a prototype-based object with vertices, edges, an _id index, and per-vertex _in and _out edge lists.
Queries are stored as a program of pipetype steps, and a gremlin traverses the graph carrying state through the pipes.
Lazy evaluation lets queries like take(10) stop early, at the cost of a more complex execution model the user must learn.
summary.summary: This chapter from the 500 Lines or Less book builds Dagoba, an in-memory graph database in JavaScript. It starts from a naive list-of-edges approach to family-tree queries, then refactors it into a namespace, a graph factory, vertex and edge insertion, and a query object. The author explains design tradeoffs such as copying versus sharing vertex data, and strict versus lazy evaluation of query steps. The page is an excerpt that ends mid-discussion of pipetype lookup, so it covers the design of the core but not the full interpreter.
